{"notes": "Visit 3 (left at 5:30). Based only on what I saw and heard; I still don't know who placed which domino.

Table: the crossing is now connected, and the upper tail loop is dark (connected) along its top and right side to about x28, y10. Still pale: the inner hook at about x26.5-28, y10-13, the right side between the notch and Hana's bottom-right bridge. The finish isn't secured.

Hana: Kept coordinating clearly. She asked for hands off her corner, tried a direct bridge, and accepted Sofia's offer. She split the work so people didn't collide. At 5:15 she said the right side was joined down to the bridge, but the pale stretch is still pale in what I saw, so I can't confirm that. Check whether it actually connects. Leadership and collaboration are strong. Execution is unproven until the loop lights up.

Sofia: Her read of the loop was specific and matched what I saw: the upper side runs out at the notch, and the pale stretch is the right side. She offered to fix the notch only after Hana's bridge, waited for Hana's word, and stayed clear of Hana's corner. That is good collaboration and sound judgment. Whether the notch fix works is still open.

Omar: Not seen or heard again. His upper tail is now largely connected, but I don't know whether he had a hand in that. Ask privately what he placed and whether he did the upper arc bridge.

Jack: Hana asked him to report if the loop lights up, and he said nothing that I heard. Still no evidence of his contribution. Ask him directly what he did and whether he was blocked.

Next: confirm what falls when the start domino is pushed, then ask each person privately who did what."}
